name: Sustainable Forests and Communities Initiative
summary: Grants of up to US$50,000 a year to charities and public bodies in forested US communities that combine forest conservation or ecological restoration with sustainable forest-based jobs and community consensus-building.

geography.label: Forested communities in the United States

fiscal_sponsor.note: With a signed agreement; the sponsor shows direct fiscal and programme oversight

reporting: Metrics on qualitative and quantitative outcomes at the end of each grant period.

eligibility.rule: Is an IRS 501(c)(3) public charity, state or political subdivision, or tribal governmental entity
A fiscal sponsor submits a signed sponsorship agreement and shows direct fiscal and program oversight
No relief/rescue, media, film, photography, books, or general-public behavior education
No capital projects; non-purchase work associated with land acquisition is allowed
No individual grants/scholarships, camps, unrelated operating costs, lobbying, endowments, start-up costs or research

calls.label: Letter of inquiry
calls.recurring: Letter of inquiry deadline is 1 January, with no year given.

recurring.quote: Please note that the Letter of Inquiry submission deadline is January 1st

applicant_types.quote: Organization must be classified by the Internal Revenue Service as a 501(c)(3) public charity or a state or political subdivision or a tribal governmental entity.

geography.quote: SFCI focuses on supporting activities in forested communities throughout the United States.

access.quote: Please carefully review our Guidelines and consider whether your organization is a strong fit with WFF's requirements and restrictions.

window.quote: Please note that the Letter of Inquiry submission deadline is January 1st

amount.quote: The maximum grant size for SFCI is $50,000 per year.

fiscal_sponsor.quote: Applications from an organization acting as a fiscal sponsor will be considered when a Fiscal Sponsorship Agreement has been signed by both parties and submitted with the application. Fiscal Sponsors must be able to demonstrate substantial and direct fiscal and program oversight.

reporting.quote: Applicants will be required to report on the program's success by providing metrics on the qualitative and quantitative outcomes at the end of each grant period.

effort.quote: By March 1st Application opens (for invited organizations). March 15th Application deadline

eligibility.quote: Organization must be classified by the Internal Revenue Service as a 501(c)(3) public charity or a state or political subdivision or a tribal governmental entity.

Applications from an organization acting as a fiscal sponsor will be considered when a Fiscal Sponsorship Agreement has been signed by both parties and submitted with the application. Fiscal Sponsors must be able to demonstrate substantial and direct fiscal and program oversight.
WFF does not accept applications from fiscal agents.
Relief and rescue programs. Programs whose purpose is to create specific media, film, photography, or books. Programs that attempt to change behavior by education of the general public.

Capital projects, including land acquisition or the construction of buildings. Note, while WFF funds cannot be used to purchase land, SFCI will fund work associated with land acquisition such as staff time, community engagement, and management planning.

Grants or scholarships to individuals. Camps or cultural exchange programs. General operating costs not connected to the project proposal. Lobbying prohibited by the Internal Revenue Code. Endowments. Start-up costs for new organizations. Research projects.

after_award.quote: Annual Renewal Grant reports must be submitted annually and will serve as the basis for a check-in conversation with trustees.
